treatment_plan.summary: 67F with known non-valvular AF (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4) on warfarin (INR 2.4) who has undergone primary PCI with DES for NSTEMI, also with T2DM. Requires a tailored antithrombotic strategy balancing thromboembolic risk, stent thrombosis risk, and bleeding risk with triple therapy. A proton pump inhibitor should be co-prescribed for gastric protection.

recommendations.intervention: Warfarin — continue lifelong for stroke prevention in non-valvular AF (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4); target INR 2.0–2.5 while on dual antiplatelet therapy
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4 has a high thromboembolic risk (adjusted stroke rate ~4.0%/year) and requires lifelong OAC; INR target should be lowered to 2.0–2.5 when combined with antiplatelet agents to reduce bleeding.

recommendations.intervention: Aspirin 75–100 mg daily orally — initial component of triple therapy post-PCI with DES for NSTEMI
recommendations.rationale: Following ACS (NSTEMI) with PCI in this AF patient at moderate-to-high stroke risk, triple therapy (VKA + aspirin + clopidogrel) is recommended in the short term (3–6 months).

recommendations.intervention: Clopidogrel 75 mg daily orally — P2Y12 inhibitor for post-PCI stent coverage and long-term antiplatelet therapy
recommendations.rationale: Clopidogrel is the P2Y12 inhibitor recommended in combination with VKA post-PCI for AF patients; it should be continued for at least 3–6 months after DES implantation for ACS, then as part of dual therapy with VKA up to 12 months.

recommendations.intervention: Proton pump inhibitor (e.g. omeprazole) — gastric protection during triple antithrombotic therapy
recommendations.rationale: Table 13 footnote states 'Gastric protection with a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) should be considered where necessary' during triple therapy in this 67F post-PCI patient on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel.

recommendations.intervention: Prasugrel — alternative P2Y12 inhibitor found more effective in diabetics undergoing PCI; consider if clopidogrel resistance suspected
recommendations.rationale: This 67F has T2DM and underwent PCI for NSTEMI; prasugrel has been found more effective than clopidogrel in diabetic patients. However, it should be given after coronary angiography and avoided if patient >75 years or <60 kg.

recommendations.intervention: Atorvastatin 80 mg daily orally — high-intensity statin for ACS post-PCI
recommendations.rationale: Early initiation of high-dose statin therapy after admission for UA/NSTEMI reduces major adverse cardiac events; this 67F with T2DM and NSTEMI post-PCI should receive high-potency statin therapy indefinitely.

recommendations.intervention: ACE inhibitor (e.g. ramipril 2.5 mg BD, target 10 mg OD) orally — for secondary prevention post-MI with diabetes
recommendations.rationale: ACE-I should be considered early for patients with diabetes post-MI; this 67F with T2DM and NSTEMI post-PCI benefits from ACE-I for cardioprotective and renoprotective effects.

recommendations.intervention: Beta-blocker (e.g. bisoprolol 1.25 mg OD, target 10 mg OD) orally — for post-MI secondary prevention
recommendations.rationale: Beta-blockers should be administered early post-NSTEMI and continued indefinitely if ischaemia is present; this 67F post-PCI for NSTEMI requires beta-blockade unless contraindicated.

recommendations.intervention: Echocardiography — assess LV function post-MI
recommendations.rationale: Echocardiogram to assess LV function is recommended in the outpatient evaluation post-UA/NSTEMI; this 67F post-PCI needs LV function assessment to guide ACE-I and beta-blocker therapy.

recommendations.intervention: INR monitoring — weekly until stable on triple therapy, then at least monthly; target INR 2.0–2.5 during triple/dual therapy
recommendations.rationale: When VKA is given in combination with clopidogrel or low-dose aspirin, careful regulation of anticoagulation dose intensity is needed with an INR range of 2.0–2.5; this 67F on warfarin requires close INR monitoring during triple therapy.

recommendations.intervention: Fasting lipid profile — assess LDL-C for statin titration post-ACS
recommendations.rationale: Assessment of a fasting lipid profile is recommended within 24 hours of hospitalisation for all UA/NSTEMI patients; this 67F with T2DM and NSTEMI needs lipid assessment to guide statin therapy and target LDL-C <2.0 mmol/L.

recommendations.intervention: Non-invasive ischaemia assessment (stress test) — post-discharge evaluation for residual ischaemia
recommendations.rationale: Low risk patients should be assessed non-invasively for ischaemia post-discharge; this 67F post-PCI needs functional assessment to guide further revascularisation decisions.

recommendations.intervention: Radial access preferred for any future invasive procedures — to reduce bleeding risk during therapeutic anticoagulation
recommendations.rationale: In anticoagulated patients at very high risk of thrombo-embolism, uninterrupted therapy with VKA is the preferred strategy and radial access should be used as the first choice even during therapeutic anticoagulation (INR 2–3); this 67F on warfarin post-PCI should have radial access preferred for any future procedures.

monitoring.schedule: Weekly until stable, then at least monthly; more frequent during triple therapy
monitoring.target: INR 2.0–2.5 during triple/dual antiplatelet therapy; INR 2.0–3.0 (target 2.5) when on VKA monotherapy

monitoring.schedule: At baseline and serially during acute admission

monitoring.parameter: Fasting lipid profile (TC, LDL-C, HDL-C, TG)
monitoring.schedule: Within 24 hours of hospitalisation, then 4–6 weeks post-discharge
Baseline, 1–2 weeks after starting ACE-I, then at least annually
During acute admission; keep blood sugars less than 8mmol/l in the acute setting

red_flags: Active bleeding or signs of haemorrhage during triple antithrombotic therapy — discontinue one antiplatelet agent and seek urgent review
INR >3.5 — increased risk of intracranial haemorrhage; withhold warfarin, seek urgent haematology review
Recurrent ischaemic chest pain post-PCI — urgent cardiology review for possible stent thrombosis or new lesion
Haemodynamic instability (SBP <90 mmHg) — withhold nitrate and beta-blocker, urgent assessment
Signs of stroke or TIA — immediate imaging and neurology review; timing of anticoagulation restart to be individualised
follow_up: 1–2 weeks post-discharge: review antithrombotic tolerance, INR stability, renal function and potassium after ACE-I initiation — adjust warfarin dose to maintain INR 2.0–2.5; if renal function deteriorates >30% or potassium ≥5.6 mmol/L, reduce or discontinue ACE-I
4–6 weeks: repeat fasting lipid profile and assess statin response — if LDL-C not at target <2.0 mmol/L, uptitrate statin or add ezetimibe

3–6 months: reassess dual/triple therapy duration — if low bleeding risk (HAS-BLED 0–2), continue triple therapy for 6 months, then switch to VKA + clopidogrel 75 mg daily up to 12 months; if high bleeding risk (HAS-BLED >3), shorten triple therapy to 4 weeks
12 months: reassess need for continued dual antiplatelet therapy — if >1 year post-ACS with no recurrent events, consider VKA monotherapy
Ongoing: lifelong VKA for AF with target INR 2.0–3.0 once off dual antiplatelet therapy; regular INR monitoring as per CPG protocol
Ongoing: annual comprehensive diabetic review including HbA1c, renal function (eGFR, UACR), lipid profile, retinopathy screening, and foot assessment
unresolved_questions: The retrieved AF CPG predates current evidence — the AF guideline does not address newer antithrombotic strategies (e.g. dual pathway with DOAC + P2Y12 inhibitor without aspirin, per WOEST, PIONEER AF-PCI, RE-DUAL PCI, AUGUSTUS trials). A current cardiology guideline check is warranted.

Prasugrel is mentioned as more effective in diabetics (chunk 5) but the specific triple therapy table (chunk 1, Table 13) only references clopidogrel — the optimal P2Y12 inhibitor choice for this 67F on warfarin post-DES requires specialist input.

Dose of aspirin during triple therapy: Table 13 specifies 'aspirin 75-100mg/day' but the NSTEMI CPG (chunk 8) states ASA maintenance dose 75–150 mg daily — clarifying the exact dose to use during triple therapy is needed.
HAS-BLED score not calculable from provided patient data — bleeding risk category (low/intermediate vs high) determines duration of triple therapy and should be formally assessed.

Metformin safety post-PCI with iodinated contrast: the CPG notes diabetics are at higher risk of contrast nephropathy (chunk 5) and recommends avoiding nephrotoxic agents including metformin peri-procedurally (Appendix VII). Renal function should be confirmed before resuming metformin.

The predicted ICD-11 code (8B26.4 — Posterior cerebral artery syndrome) does not match the clinical scenario of NSTEMI post-PCI with AF. The primary diagnosis should be revised to reflect the actual clinical presentation.
